text:
maria: Heads-up — customer requested expanded audit coverage for RBAC changes + KMS key usage across dedicated/private. They want per-API-key and per-role events retained for 90 days and validated on ingest. Can we scope perf/cost impact?

 dave: @maria got it. high-level: per-event KMS decrypt for every envelope will blow costs. We should consider envelope encryption with a single per-batch KMS call.

 oliver: Also seeing backpressure in the ingest queue when we turn on verbose audit for a tenant in prod. audit-bot logged spikes yesterday:

 ```
WARN ingest-queue: backlog=12k items, avg-latency=800ms, ES-index-rate=75/s
WARN kv-cache: evictions=240/s
```

 jen: If we batch at the SDK proxy (100 events/batch) and do one envelope key unwrap per-batch, that reduces KMS ops ~100x. But adds latency for first-event in batch. SLA tradeoff.

 maria: Proposed options: 1) sample 1:10 for full payloads + store digests for all events, 2) batch-unwrap + archive raw events to S3 for on-demand retrieval, 3) keep full stream and pay cost (not ideal). Thoughts? :thinking_face:

 kevin: For indexing cost we should push minimal indexed fields: actor, action, resource, timestamp, role_delta. Put full JSON in cold storage (S3) with pointer in ES to reduce ES document size. That will knock down storage/indexing cost dramatically.

 dave: Agree. Also suggest per-tenant ingestion tiers and soft QPS caps. When a tenant flips verbose auditing on, we queue them into a higher-cost pipeline with autoscaled workers and explicit rate limits to avoid cluster-wide pressure.

 oliver: One more: schema change we need to add `rbac_change.type` and `rbac_change.scope` fields so queries are reliable. Example mapping (rough):

 ```json
"rbac_change.type": { "type": "keyword" },
"rbac_change.scope": { "type": "keyword" },
"actor.role_before": { "type": "keyword" },
"actor.role_after": { "type": "keyword" }
```

 maria: @oliver can you open a small PR to the ingest pipeline adding those fields and a migration doc for ES mapping? We should also add a migration plan that reindexes only the last 30d.

 jen: On validation: customer expects event-level signature using the tenant's signing key. That implies extra crypto per-event. We can validate asynchronously: accept events, enqueue for async signature validation and reject on failure with a corrective action. Avoid sync crypto on hot path.

 audit-bot: incident-notice: tenant-abc triggered audit-throttle at 2026-02-12T14:03:21Z — autoscale initiated.

 kevin: Cost estimates ballpark: full-indexing verbose = +$4k/month per high-volume tenant; batch+archive pattern = +$450/month. KMS envelope unwraps cost ~ $0.03 per 10k ops if batched vs $3 per 10k if per-event. Need exact numbers from finance.

 maria: Action items: @oliver PR for mapping + migration plan, @dave design for batch-unwrap pipeline and tenant tiers, @jen async validation flow doc, @kevin S3 archival retention policy & cost calc. I'll consolidate and share with the customer.

 dave: I'll prototype a small PoC for batch-unwrap and push metrics (KMS ops, ingest latency). ETA EOD Friday.

 jen: I'll write the async validation spec and failure mode playbook (how we notify customers & remediate).

 maria: Great. Quick Q — do we want to offer a managed 'audit-heavy' addon in billing or fold into Dedicated? Could be a revenue stream.

 kevin: Strong yes on addon. Makes cost transparent.

 oliver: Noted. I'll start the PR now.

 maria: Thanks team. I'll drop a short summary in the customer thread after we have the PoC numbers. :thumbsup:
